title: Data protection principles for AI
summary: Apply lawfulness, fairness, transparency, purpose limitation, minimization, accuracy, storage limitation, security and accountability to training and use.

title: Lawful basis
summary: Identify a lawful basis for each processing purpose in development and deployment; legitimate interest needs a documented three-step test (EDPB Opinion 28/2024).
evidence: Legitimate interest assessments; lawful basis register.

title: Special category data
summary: Process sensitive data only under an Article 9(2) condition; see also AI Act Art. 4a for bias correction.

title: Transparency to individuals
summary: Tell people how their data is used for AI, including sources when not collected from them.

title: Data subject rights
summary: Handle access, rectification, erasure and objection requests, including for training data where applicable.

title: Automated decision-making
summary: Respect limits on solely automated decisions with legal or similar effects; offer human intervention and the right to contest.

title: Data protection by design and default
summary: Build privacy into AI design: minimization, pseudonymization, access limits.

title: Processors
summary: Contracts with AI vendors processing personal data on your behalf.

title: Security
summary: Appropriate security for AI data and models, including AI-specific attacks.

title: Data protection impact assessment
summary: Run a DPIA for high-risk AI processing; can be linked to the AI Act FRIA.

title: Anonymity of AI models
summary: Do not assume a model trained on personal data is anonymous; assess case by case.
